alignments.note: Passive participle as predicate of a verbless clause, with the construction-supplied copula joining it (rule 20), headed on the word carrying the lexeme.
Subject of the clause takes only its own word (rule 20).
Multi-word preposition headed on the word carrying the lexeme (rule 24).
Anarthrous participle taking the supplied relative that makes it an English noun phrase, headed on the word carrying the lexeme (rule 46).
Bare place name with the preposition the ASV supplies to state what it contributes to the clause; the word belongs to the nominal and is never the head (rule 33).
Short divine name rendered *Jehovah*; the margin's *Hallelujah* gloss is read and set aside under rule 38.

review_notes: The supplied *at* before Jerusalem goes to the bare nominal under rule 33, no preposition morpheme standing there.
*Who dwelleth* is the anarthrous participle's own supplied noun phrase (rule 46), unlike the `added` relatives of vv. 7 and 9, which stand over finite clauses.
